key_insight: A deterministic software pipeline can convert qualitative post-stroke syndromic observations into structured, reproducible cognitive profiles across 10 domains.
clinical_relevance: This could shorten documentation time in acute stroke care while producing auditable reports that better capture focal neurocognitive deficits than standard screening alone.
method: Retrospective analysis of a prospective acute stroke registry (n = 169).
NeuroDraft used a deterministic Python scoring core with a 10-domain Luria Raw matrix plus constrained text generation for reporting.
Statistical validation included internal consistency testing, Kruskal-Wallis comparisons, and principal component analysis.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports good internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha = 0.85) and strong domain discrimination across baseline mental status tiers, with a primary factor explaining 41.26% of variance.
watch_item: Because this is a retrospective single-platform evaluation, real-world generalizability, external validation, and workflow impact in diverse stroke settings still need confirmation.
paper_title: Algorithmic Multi-Domain Syndromic Profiling in Cerebrovascular Disease: A Deterministic Approach to Post-Stroke Neurocognitive Deficit Mapping
